questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the function of dietary fibre in the human diet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aids Digestion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dietary fibre**, also known as roughage or bulk, is primarily found in plant-based foods such as fruits, vegetables, whole grains, nuts, and seeds.
 
• It is a type of carbohydrate that is not digestible by human enzymes, meaning it passes through the digestive system relatively intact.
 
• One of the primary functions of dietary fibre is to **aid digestion** by adding bulk to the stool, which helps prevent constipation and promotes regular bowel movements.
 
• Dietary fibre can help maintain a healthy gut microbiome by serving as food for beneficial gut bacteria, which produce short-chain fatty acids that contribute to gut health.
 
• Soluble fibre can help regulate blood sugar levels and lower cholesterol by slowing the absorption of sugar and binding to cholesterol in the digestive tract, though these benefits are secondary to its primary role in digestion.
 
• It does not provide energy directly, as it is not broken down into glucose, nor does it contribute to muscle building or increase cholesterol levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Dietary Fibre:**

 
 
• **Soluble fibre:** Found in foods like oats, barley, and fruits such as apples and citrus. It dissolves in water and forms a gel-like substance that can help lower cholesterol and stabilize blood sugar levels.
 
• **Insoluble fibre:** Found in foods like whole grains, nuts, seeds, and vegetables. It does not dissolve in water and primarily adds bulk to stool, aiding in regular bowel movements and preventing constipation.
 
 
 
• **Health Benefits:**
 
 
• Consuming adequate dietary fibre can help prevent several digestive disorders such as **diverticular disease**, **irritable bowel syndrome** (IBS), and **constipation**.
 
• Dietary fibre is associated with a lower risk of chronic diseases such as **type 2 diabetes**, **heart disease**, and **certain types of cancer**, particularly colorectal cancer.
 
• It can contribute to weight management by promoting a feeling of fullness, thereby reducing overall calorie intake.
 
 
 
• **Recommended Intake:**
 
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** recommends adults consume at least **25-30 grams** of dietary fibre daily from a variety of food sources.
 
• Children and adolescents require slightly less depending on their age, ranging from **15-25 grams per day**.
 
 
 
• **Examples of High-Fibre Foods:**
 
 
• Whole grains like **brown rice**, **quinoa**, and **whole wheat bread**.
 
• Legumes such as **lentils**, **chickpeas**, and **black beans**.
 
• Fruits such as **bananas**, **apples**, and **berries**.
 
• Vegetables like **broccoli**, **carrots**, and **spinach**.
 
• Nuts and seeds such as **almonds**, **chia seeds**, and **flaxseeds**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Misconceptions about Dietary Fibre:**

 
 
• Dietary fibre does not directly provide **energy** or **calories** because it is not digestible.
 
• It does not help build **muscle**, as its function is primarily related to digestion and gut health.
 
• While dietary fibre can lower **cholesterol**, it does not increase it.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends:**
 
 
• Many regions, including **North America** and **Europe**, report a significant fibre deficiency in their diets, often due to the prevalence of processed foods.
 
• Countries such as **India** and **China**, with diets rich in grains, legumes, and vegetables, typically meet or exceed recommended fibre levels.
 
 
 
• **Practical Tips for Increasing Fibre Intake:**
 
 
• Replace refined grains with **whole grains**, such as switching from white bread to whole wheat bread.
 
• Add more **fruits** and **vegetables** to meals and snacks.
 
• Incorporate **nuts**, **seeds**, and **legumes** into daily meals.
 
• Hydrate adequately, as fibre requires water to move effectively through the digestive system.

questions.question: If i is the angle of incidence and r is the angle of refraction, which relation is correct according to Snell’s law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sin i ÷ sin r = constant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Snell's law states that the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence (i) to the sine of the angle of refraction (r) is constant for a given pair of media and is equal to the refractive index.
 
• The mathematical expression for Snell's law is **sin i ÷ sin r = n**, where **n** is the refractive index of the second medium with respect to the first.
 
• This law explains the bending of light when it passes from one medium to another with a different refractive index.
 
• Snell's law is crucial in understanding optical phenomena such as refraction and total internal reflection.
 
• The constant value (n) depends on the optical density of the two media involved in the transition of light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refractive Index (n):**

 
 
• The refractive index is a dimensionless quantity that describes how light propagates through a medium.
 
• It is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in the medium: **n = c/v**.
 
 
 
• **Angle of Incidence (i):**
 
 
• This is the angle between the incident ray and the normal (perpendicular) to the surface at the point of incidence.
 
 
 
• **Angle of Refraction (r):**
 
 
• This is the angle between the refracted ray and the normal to the surface at the point of refraction.
 
 
 
• **Total Internal Reflection:**
 
 
• This phenomenon occurs when the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle, causing the light to reflect entirely within the denser medium.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Snell's Law:**
 
 
• Used in designing lenses, prisms, and optical instruments like microscopes and telescopes.
 
• Essential in fiber optic communication for guiding light signals through cables.

questions.question: Two resistors, one of 20 Ω and the other of 30 Ω are connected in parallel. This combination is connected in series with an 8 Ω resistor and a 12 V battery. The current in the 30 Ω resistor is __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.24 A.**__

 
• 20 ohms and 30 ohms resistors are connected in parallel,

∴** Resistance in Parallel, 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂**

Resultant 1/R= 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12 = 12 ohms

∴ Total resistance = 8 + 12 = 20 ohms

 
• Ohm’s Law,

⇒ **I = V/R**

⇒ I = 12/20

⇒ I = 0.6 Amp.

 
• The voltage drop across 12 ohms is 12×0.6 = 7.2 volts
 
• Current in 30 ohms resistor is 7.2/30 = **0.24 A**

questions.question: Why are soft drink and soda water bottles sealed under high pressure in beverage industries?

options.text: To decrease the amount of sugar
To increase the solubility of carbon dioxide

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To increase the solubility of carbon dioxide.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Soft drink and soda bottles** are sealed under high pressure specifically to enhance the **solubility of carbon dioxide (CO₂)** in the liquid. Under high pressure, CO₂ dissolves more efficiently, creating the fizzy texture that is characteristic of carbonated beverages.
 
• At lower pressures, carbon dioxide escapes from the liquid, leading to a loss of the signature fizz and carbonation. Hence, sealing under high pressure ensures long-lasting carbonation. *This statement is correct.*
 
• The process of sealing bottles under high pressure is an application of **Henry's Law**, which states that the amount of gas dissolved in a liquid is directly proportional to the pressure of the gas above the liquid. *Hence, this principle supports the practice in beverage industries.*
 
• Soft drink companies use this technique to maintain the desired taste, as the dissolved CO₂ contributes to the tangy taste and fizzy sensation. Without sealing the bottles under pressure, the drink would lose its flavor and appeal. *This is an important factor for customer satisfaction.*
 
• Other options mentioned in the question, such as increasing temperature, preventing freezing, or decreasing the amount of sugar, are irrelevant to the carbonation process. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Henry's Law:**

 
 
• **Henry's Law** states that the amount of gas that dissolves in a liquid is proportional to the pressure of the gas in contact with the liquid. This is why soft drink manufacturers utilize high pressure to dissolve CO₂ effectively.
 
• When the bottle is opened, the pressure is released, and CO₂ escapes in the form of bubbles, creating the fizz that we enjoy.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Carbonation:**
 
 
• **Carbonated beverages** like soda, sparkling water, and soft drinks rely on this process to enhance taste and texture.
 
• The carbonation process also plays a role in beverages such as **beer** and **champagne**, where natural fermentation creates CO₂.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Pressure:**
 
 
• High-pressure sealing ensures **long-term storage** of carbonated drinks without losing their fizz.
 
• It also prevents microbial growth as CO₂ creates an acidic environment, extending the shelf life of the beverage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Incorrect Options:**

 
 
• Increasing the temperature does not contribute to carbonation. In fact, higher temperatures reduce CO₂ solubility.
 
• Preventing freezing is not relevant to soft drink bottling under pressure. Freezing is controlled through storage conditions.
 
• Decreasing the amount of sugar is unrelated to the carbonation process. Sugar content is determined by the recipe for taste.
 
 
 
• **Global Practices:**
 
 
• **Beverage manufacturers worldwide** use similar techniques to preserve the fizz in carbonated drinks, adhering to industry standards.
 
• The use of CO₂ in beverages is regulated by food safety authorities like the **FDA** in the **United States** and **FSSAI** in **India**.

questions.question: The large carnivores or the tertiary consumers exist at which level on the food chain?
questions.solution:
A food chain shows how the organisms are related with each other by the food they eat. Each level of a food chain represents a different trophic level. Animals that come of 4th level include tigers, lions etc.

__**Explanation-**__

A food chain refers to the sequence of events in an ecosystem, where one organism eats another and then is eaten by another organism. It's a straightforward way to understand the flow of energy and nutrients in a specific ecosystem. Here is a more detailed explanation:

 
• **Producers:** These are usually plants, which sit at the base of every food chain. Plants capture solar energy from the sun through the process of photosynthesis and use it to convert water and carbon dioxide into glucose (a type of sugar). Plants then use this glucose as their food/energy source for growth and reproduction. This energy gets transferred through the food chain when plants are eaten by other organisms.
 
• **Primary Consumers:** These are herbivores – animals that eat plants. Examples include rabbits, cows, and giraffes. They consume producers and get their energy from them.
 
• **Secondary Consumers**: These are carnivores (meat-eaters) and omnivores (animals that eat both animals and plants). They eat primary consumers. Examples include foxes, snakes, and humans.
 
• **Tertiary Consumers:** These are animals that eat secondary consumers. They are typically carnivorous predators. Lions and tigers, which can eat foxes or snakes, fit in this category.
 
• **Decomposers: **Finally, decomposers, like fungi and bacteria, break down all categories of dead organisms, and in the process, they return nutrients to the soil, which can be used by producers, thus cycling the nutrients back into the ecosystem.

This creates a "chain" effect – where energy moves up the levels from producer to consumer and eventually to decomposers.

questions.question: Which meristematic tissue is found at nodes and helps in regrowth of grasses?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Intercalary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Intercalary meristem is a type of meristematic tissue located at the nodes of plants.
 
• It is responsible for the regrowth of grasses and contributes to the elongation of internodes.
 
• Intercalary meristems allow rapid regeneration in grasses after grazing or mowing.
 
• This tissue is present in monocots, particularly in grasses, which aids their survival in environments with regular disturbances.
 
• Unlike apical meristem, which is found at the tips of roots and shoots, intercalary meristem is strategically located at the base of nodes and leaf blades.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meristematic Tissue:**

 
 
• Meristematic tissues are responsible for the growth of plants and consist of actively dividing cells.
 
• These tissues are classified into apical, lateral, and intercalary based on their location.
 
• Apical meristem contributes to the primary growth at the tips of roots and shoots.
 
• Lateral meristem is involved in secondary growth, leading to an increase in the girth of the plant.
 
 
 
• **Monocots vs. Dicots:**
 
 
• Monocots, like grasses, have intercalary meristems that help them regrow quickly after damage.
 
• Dicots generally lack intercalary meristems and rely on apical and lateral meristems for growth.
 
 
 
• **Node and Internode:**
 
 
• Nodes are points on the stem where leaves or branches originate.
 
• Internodes are the regions between two nodes, which elongate due to intercalary meristem activity.
 
 
 
• **Adaptation in Grasses:**
 
 
• Grasses are adapted to survive grazing, fire, or mowing due to the presence of intercalary meristems.
 
• These tissues regenerate leaf blades and stems quickly, ensuring survival and growth.

questions.question: In reflex action, reflex arch is formed by
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Receptor → Spinal cord → Muscle.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• In the reflex action, the reflex arch is formed by Receptor → Spinal cord → Muscle.
 
• The correct circuit of the reflex arc is Receptor→sensory neuron→spinal cord→motor neuron→effector
 
• A **reflex arc is a neural pathway that controls a reflex action. In vertebrates, instead of passing directly to the brain, the sensory neuron's synapse in the spinal cord.
 
• This helps in a faster reflex action** without the delay that is caused by routing signals through the brain.
 
• The three main types of neurons are sensory, motor and relay neurons.

The **detailed process is**

 
• The receptor detects a stimulus.
 
• Sensory neurons send electrical impulses to a relay neuron located in the spinal cord.
 
• Relay neurons connect sensory neurons to motor neurons.
 
• Motor neurons send an electrical impulse to an effector.
 
• Effector produces a response.

questions.question: A 2,000 kg truck moving at 10 m/s strikes a car waiting at a traffic light. After the collision, the two move together at 8 m/s. The mass of the car is _____ if total energy before and after collision remain conserved.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• The type of collision in which the total kinetic energy of the system remains constant before and after the collision is called elastic collision or perfectly elastic collision.
 
• As there is no net external force on the system, so momentum before the collision and after the collision will remain same.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/53f30ff565a8f800a775a33f3e7f8e7ba67f31484026846af180f2c9b88f236c.png] 

Linear Momentum before collision (P1) = Linear Momentum after the collision (P2)

P1 = m1u1 + m2u2

P2 = m1v1 + m2v2

m1u1 + m2u2 = m1v1 + m2v2

 
• The kinetic energy of the system before the collision is equal to kinetic energy of the system after the collision.

KE1 = Kinetic energy before the collision and KE2 = Kinetic energy after the collision

K{E₁} = (1)/(2){m₁}u₁² + (1)/(2){m₂}u₂² = K{E₂} = (1)/(2){m₁}v₁² + (1)/(2) {m₂}v₂²

EXPLANATION__:

Given that,

Mass of the truck (m₁) = 2000 kg

Velocity of the truck (v₁) = 10 m/s

Mass of the car = m₂

Velocity of car before collision v₂ = 0 m/s

The final velocity of car and truck after collision (Vf) = 8 m/s.

If the total kinetic energy and momentum in the system remain constant in a collision, then such collision is called Elastic collision.

By conservation of momentum i.e. final momentum is equal to initial momentum.

Initial momentum will me p₁ = m₁v₁ + m₂ v₂

⇒ (2000 × 10) + (m₂ × 0)

⇒ 20000

As initial momentum is equal to final momentum

We get p₁ = p₂

Where p₂ = (m₁ + m₂) × vf

⇒ 20000 = (2000 + m₂) × 8

⇒ 2500 = 2000 + m₂

⇒ m₂ = 500

The mass of the car is **500 kg**

questions.question: What are the units for base quantities called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental or base units**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Base quantities are physical quantities that are defined independently and are used as the foundation for other derived quantities.
 
• The units for these base quantities are known as **fundamental or base units**.
 
• Examples of base units include the meter (m) for length, kilogram (kg) for mass, and second (s) for time.
 
• The **International System of Units (SI)** is the globally accepted standard that defines these fundamental units.
 
• The SI system includes seven base units, which are used worldwide for scientific and technical purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Base Quantities:**

 
 
• These are quantities like length, mass, time, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity.
 
• They are considered independent and form the foundation of the measurement system.
 
 
 
• **SI Base Units:**
 
 
• The seven SI base units are: meter (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), ampere (A), kelvin (K), mole (mol), and candela (cd).
 
• Each unit corresponds to one of the seven base quantities.
 
 
 
• **Derived Units:**
 
 
• Derived units are formed by combining base units according to the relationships between physical quantities.
 
• Examples include the newton (N) for force and the joule (J) for energy.
 
 
 
• **History of SI Units:**
 
 
• The SI system was officially adopted in 1960 at the 11th General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM).
 
• It has since become the most widely used measurement system globally.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Standard Units:**
 
 
• Standardized units ensure consistency and comparability in measurements across different regions and disciplines.
 
• They are crucial for scientific research, trade, and technological development.

questions.question: Which of the following gases is also known as a 'Stranger' gas?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Xenon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xenon(Xe)** is a component of zero-valence elements called noble or inert gases.
 
• It is inert to most normal chemical reactions (e.g. combustion) since the outer valence shell contains eight electrons.
 
• This results in a stable, minimum energy configuration in which the outer electrons are tightly bound.
 
• **The first published report confirming xenon anaesthesia was published in 1946 by the American medical researcher John H. Lawrence.**
 
• Xenon has been undiscovered for a very long time, although it is present in traces in the atmosphere.** It is still a subject of interest due to its reactivity with many elements in a specialised and regulated environment, hence the name "Stranger Gas."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Neon** is a chemical element with the Ne symbol and atomic number 10. It is a noble gas. Neon is a colourless, odourless, inert monatomic gas under normal conditions, with an air density of around two-thirds.
 
• **Krypton **is a chemical element with the Kr symbol and atomic number 36. It is a colourless, odourless, tasteless noble gas that exists in trace quantities in the atmosphere and is mostly used in fluorescent lamps with other rare gases.
 
• **Argon** is a chemical element with a symbol of Ar and an atomic number 18. It is a periodic table in group 18 and is a noble gas. Argon is the third most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere, at 0.934 per cent (9340 ppmv).

questions.question: If a current of 1.5 A is maintained in a resistor of 10 Ohm, then the energy dissipated in the resistor in 1 minute will be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1350 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Given: Current (I) = 1.5 A, Resistance (R) = 10 Ω, Time (t) = 1 minute = 60 seconds.
 
• Formula for energy dissipated: **H = I²Rt**, where H is heat energy in joules (J).
 
• Substituting: H = (1.5)² × 10 × 60 = 2.25 × 10 × 60 = **1350 J**.
 
• Since 1 joule/second = 1 watt, total energy dissipated in 1 minute is **1350 J = 1350 W·s**.
 
• Hence, energy dissipated is **1350 joules**, which matches option 1 numerically (not unit-wise, see clarification below).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Power (P)**

 
 
• P = I²R is the instantaneous power dissipated in a resistor.
 
• Here, P = (1.5)² × 10 = 22.5 W (this is rate, not total energy).
 
 
 
• **Energy (E) vs Power (P)**
 
 
• Energy = Power × Time.
 
• Power is the rate at which energy is used; energy is the total work done or heat dissipated.
 
 
 
• **Joule's Law of Heating:**
 
 
• Heat produced in resistor is proportional to square of current, resistance, and time (H = I²Rt).
 
 
 
• **Unit Conversions:**
 
 
• 1 J = 1 W·s; 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.
 
• In this question, energy is asked, so answer should be in joules, not watts.
 
 
 
• **Correct Unit Clarification:**
 
 
• The numeric value 1350 is correct for energy in joules, but **W (watt)** is a unit of power, not energy.
 
• The most precise answer should be **1350 J (Joules)**,

questions.question: The primary force responsible for pulling water upward in tall plants is ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**transpiration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Transpiration** is the process by which water evaporates from the aerial parts of plants, primarily through the stomata present in leaves.
 
• The evaporation of water creates a negative pressure or suction force, known as the **transpiration pull**, which helps to draw water upward through the xylem vessels.
 
• Transpiration plays a crucial role in maintaining the flow of water and nutrients from the roots to the leaves and other parts of the plant.
 
• This process is most significant in tall plants, where the force generated by transpiration pull is essential to overcome gravity and transport water to the top.
 
• Environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, wind, and light intensity influence the rate of transpiration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xylem**

 
 
• Xylem is the vascular tissue responsible for transporting water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
• It consists of specialized cells such as tracheids and vessel elements that facilitate the movement of water.
 
• The cohesion and adhesion properties of water molecules play a key role in maintaining the continuous water column in xylem vessels.
 
 
 
• **Root Pressure**
 
 
• Root pressure is a positive pressure generated by the active absorption of nutrients and water by root cells.
 
• Although root pressure contributes to water movement, it is insufficient for tall plants and is only effective in smaller plants.
 
 
 
• **Guttation**
 
 
• Guttation is the exudation of water droplets from the edges of leaves, typically occurring at night or under conditions of high soil moisture and low transpiration.
 
• It should not be confused with transpiration, which is the evaporation of water vapor from plant surfaces.
 
 
 
• **Osmosis**
 
 
• Osmosis is the passive movement of water molecules across a semi-permeable membrane from a region of low solute concentration to a region of high solute concentration.
 
• While osmosis is critical for water absorption by root cells, it does not contribute to the upward movement of water in tall plants.

questions.question: In the substitution of methane with chlorine, sunlight is required to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**initiate free radical formation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sunlight provides energy in the form of ultraviolet (UV) radiation, which is essential to break the bond between chlorine molecules (Cl₂) and initiate the process of free radical formation.
 
• Free radicals are highly reactive species required for the chain reaction of methane substitution.
 
• The reaction begins with the homolytic cleavage of chlorine (Cl₂) under the influence of UV light, producing chlorine free radicals.
 
• These chlorine free radicals attack methane (CH₄), leading to the formation of methyl radicals and hydrogen chloride (HCl).
 
• This chain reaction results in successive substitutions where methane reacts with chlorine to form chlorinated products such as chloromethane, dichloromethane, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Free Radical:**

 
 
• A free radical is an atom or molecule that contains an unpaired electron, making it highly reactive.
 
• In chemical reactions, free radicals play a crucial role in initiating chain processes.
 
 
 
• **Homolytic Cleavage:**
 
 
• Homolytic cleavage refers to the breaking of a bond where each atom retains one electron, forming two free radicals.
 
• This process is often facilitated by UV light or heat.
 
 
 
• **Substitution Reaction:**
 
 
• Substitution reactions involve the replacement of one atom or group in a molecule with another atom or group.
 
• In this case, chlorine atoms replace hydrogen atoms in methane during the reaction.
 
 
 
• **Photochemical Reaction:**
 
 
• A photochemical reaction is initiated by the absorption of light energy, typically UV or visible light.
 
• The substitution of methane with chlorine is a classic example of a photochemical reaction.
 
 
 
• **Reaction Products:**
 
 
• Depending on the extent of substitution, products such as chloromethane (CH₃Cl), dichloromethane (CH₂Cl₂), trichloromethane (CHCl₃), and tetrachloromethane(CHCl3) can be formed.

questions.question: In a terrestrial ecosystem, green plants capture approximately what percentage of solar energy falling on their leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem capture approximately **1% of the solar energy** that falls on their leaves and convert it into chemical energy via photosynthesis.
 
• Most of the solar energy (about 99%) is either reflected or absorbed as heat and is not utilized by plants.
 
• This captured energy forms the base of the food chain and supports all trophic levels in the ecosystem.
 
• The process of energy capture by plants is essential for the functioning of ecosystems, as it drives primary production.
 
• The efficiency of energy capture and its conversion into biomass varies depending on factors like plant species, climate, and environmental conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photosynthesis**

 
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to produce glucose and oxygen.
 
• The chemical energy stored in glucose serves as the primary energy source for most living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Gross Primary Productivity (GPP)**
 
 
• GPP refers to the total amount of energy captured by green plants through photosynthesis in a given area and time.
 
• A significant portion of this energy is used by plants for respiration.
 
 
 
• **Net Primary Productivity (NPP)**
 
 
• NPP is the energy remaining after plants use a portion of GPP for respiration.
 
• NPP = GPP - Respiration; it represents the energy available to herbivores and higher trophic levels.
 
 
 
• **Energy Flow in Ecosystems**
 
 
• Energy flows through ecosystems in a unidirectional manner, starting from producers to various trophic levels (herbivores, carnivores, decomposers).
 
• Approximately 90% of energy is lost as heat at each trophic level due to metabolic processes.
 
 
 
• **Terrestrial Ecosystems**
 
 
• These ecosystems are land-based ecosystems, such as forests, grasslands, deserts, and tundras.
 
• The primary producers in terrestrial ecosystems are green plants, which form the foundation of the food web.

questions.question: What happens to the speed of sound in a medium when its temperature increases?

options.text: It is not affected by the temperature.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It increases.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The s**peed of sound in a medium increases with the rise in temperature because the molecules of the medium move faster**, enhancing the transmission of sound waves.
 
• In gases, the speed of sound is directly proportional to the square root of the absolute temperature (**v ∝ √T**), as per the formula **v = √(γRT/M)**, where T is the temperature in Kelvin.
 
• An increase in temperature reduces the density of the medium, which also contributes to the increased speed of sound.
 
• For **every 1°C rise in temperature**, the **speed of sound in air increases by approximately** **0.6 m/s**.
 
• The relationship between speed of sound and temperature is particularly significant in gases but less pronounced in liquids and solids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed of Sound:**

 
 
• The speed of sound depends on the medium through which it travels: it is fastest in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases.
 
• For example, in air at 20°C, the speed of sound is approximately 343 m/s, while in water, it is around 1,480 m/s, and in steel, it is about 5,960 m/s.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Speed of Sound:**
 
 
• **Temperature:** Higher temperatures lead to a higher speed of sound due to increased molecular activity.
 
• **Density:** Lower density usually results in higher speeds in gases, while in solids and liquids, the relationship is more complex.
 
• **Elasticity:** A medium with higher elasticity transmits sound faster.
 
 
 
• **Formula for Speed of Sound in Gases:**
 
 
• The formula is **v = √(γRT/M)**, where:
 
 
• **γ:** Adiabatic index (ratio of specific heats).
 
• **R:** Universal gas constant.
 
• **T:** Absolute temperature in Kelvin.
 
• **M:** Molar mass of the gas.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• Understanding the speed of sound is crucial in fields like meteorology, aviation, and acoustics.
 
• The temperature dependence of sound speed is used in weather forecasting and studying atmospheric layers.

questions.question: What happens with the force of gravitation between two objects when the mass of one object is doubled?

options.text: The force of gravitation is four times
The force of gravitation is doubled
The force of gravitation is tripled
The force of gravitation is halved

questions.solution:
The force of gravitation between two objects** __Doubled__ **when the mass of one object is doubled.

As we know the Gravitational force between two objects

**F=GM₁M₂/R²**

Where G= Gravitational constant

 F= force between two objects on r distance

 M₁= mass of one object

 M₂=mass of the second object

 R= distance between both objects

If the mass of one object is doubled then let mass becomes 2M₁

So New Force= **G2M₁M₂/R²**

= 2(**GM₁M₂/R²**)

= __**2 F**__

So the force of gravitation between two objects __**Doubled** __when the mass of one object is doubled.

questions.question: Arthritis is the disease of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Joints__**.

__
 
• **Arthritis is the disease of Joints**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arthritis:**

 
 
• The main symptoms of Arthritis are the swelling and tenderness of our joints.
 
• The other symptoms of arthritis are joint pain and stiffness, which typically become worsen with age.
 
• Arthritis occurs when your body's immune system attacks the tissues of the body.
 
• There are two most common types of arthritis:
 
 
• **Osteoarthritis:** Most common type of Arthritis.
 
• **Rheumatoid arthritis:** Caused due to attack of the immune system on part of our body.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Skin:** 

 
 
• ​The most common form of skin disease is

 
 
• Acne
 
• Eczema
 
• Psoriasis 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Kidney: **
 
 
• **​**The most common form of kidney disease is chronic kidney disease. 
 
 
• Type 1 or type 2 diabetes
 
• High blood pressure
 
 
 
 
 
• **Liver: **
 
 
• **​**The most common types of liver infection are hepatitis viruses, including: 
 
 
• Hepatitis A
 
• Hepatitis B
 
• Hepatitis C
